title: Notify WorkSafe of dangerous goods above notifiable quantities
what: Make sure WorkSafe Victoria is notified when dangerous goods above the notifiable quantities in Schedule 2 are stored or handled at the premises.

sources.title: Dangerous Goods (Storage and Handling) Regulations 2022 (Vic)
sources.publisher: Victorian Legislation (authorised version saved by the owner)
sources.locator: r 64(1) (S.R. No. 115/2022, authorised version unnumbered, saved by the owner)
sources.quote: (1) An occupier of premises where notifiable goods are present must ensure that the Authority is provided with a notification of the presence of those goods that complies with subregulation (2).

sources.title: Dangerous Goods (Storage and Handling) Regulations 2022 (Vic)
sources.publisher: Victorian Legislation (authorised version saved by the owner)
sources.locator: r 5, definition of notifiable goods (S.R. No. 115/2022, authorised version unnumbered, saved by the owner)
sources.quote: notifiable goods means dangerous goods that are stored and handled in quantities that exceed the relevant quantities specified in column 5 in the table in Schedule 2

administration.note: Receives the notification and enforces the duty.

sources.title: Summary of the OHS Act 2004: General OHS Duties
sources.locator: Duties of employers to employees and contractors (section 21)
sources.quote: The OHS Act requires all employers to provide and maintain a working environment that is safe and without risks to health. This duty is to be met so far as is reasonably practicable.

triggers.note: When dangerous goods stored and handled at the premises exceed the notifiable quantities (Schedule 2, column 5).

reach.condition: if it stores or handles dangerous goods above the notifiable quantities
reach.note: Any business that holds hazardous chemicals above the manifest quantities, in any industry; most often chemical manufacturing, fuel, mining, agriculture and warehousing.

confidence_note: Quoted from the authorised PDF the owner saved from the Victorian register (data/raw/vic_legislation/, not committed); the register's documents disallow automated fetching. Victoria regulates these under its Dangerous Goods Act 1985 and its own regulations, not the model WHS law; the copy the owner saved carries no version number.

assessment.summary: A business storing or handling hazardous chemicals above set (manifest) quantities must tell the work safety regulator, or in WA license the site. It adds paperwork, and in WA a licence and fee, for larger stores.

marks.reason: Notice to the regulator (in WA, a site licence) adds paperwork and cost for sites holding large quantities.

assessment.confidence_note: Marked from the duty's design against the framework's guide; the safety benefit is not counted by the framework.
